description: Desktop permissions. Files: the page may read a file and write a file only where the person picked it in a native dialog this session — the dialog plugin adds exactly that path to the fs scope at runtime, so the static fs:scope allows nothing on its own. An imported file is read as raw bytes (fs:allow-read-file) so a bank statement in Windows-1251 can be decoded on our side. The scheduled backups and the cloud-folder sync file are NOT written through the fs plugin: a folder picked once has to stay writable after a restart, which used to mean read/write/remove over the whole home directory for any script in the page. They go through the app's own Rust commands (src-tauri/src/folder_files.rs), which only touch files with the app's own names (financeapps-backup-*.json, financeapps-sync.enc) directly inside the given folder and refuse symlinks — so no other file can be read, overwritten or deleted through them. The deny list stays as a second line for dialog-picked paths. The opener scope is pinned to this project's releases. The http scope ends with https://* and https://*:* because the sync server's address is typed by its owner at runtime and cannot be pinned at build time; it belongs to the main webview, so the defence is keeping foreign scripts out of the page: the CSP admits only the app's own bundled scripts (script-src 'self' plus the hashes and nonces Tauri adds for inline scripts at build time — no 'unsafe-inline'), and no user or server data is rendered as HTML.
